While this incident has never been fully uncovered, what we do know is that Frenchy was forced to be involved in terrible and depraved acts. As he aged, Frenchy found that he had supernatural powers. He had a rare ability to know things he’d never studied, and he was incredibly strong without ever having strength trained. His father pressed him not to join the army, so Frenchy left home and moved to Warren, Massachusetts. He married in 1985, and the couple lived on a farm. That’s where the paranormal activity started to happen. Random spots of blood began appearing across the house. Neither Frenchy nor his wife could explain where they came from. But that wasn’t even the strangest thing; they also began to witness things vanish before their very eyes and hear eerie voices throughout the home. Fires broke out all over the farm, never explained. Frenchy started to worry that something more ominous might happen to him and his wife, so he brought his guns down to the sheriff’s department and asked them to hold onto the weapons for safe-keeping. Frenchy was right. More ominous things did start to happen. In fact, they began to happen to Frenchy, himself. His being became transitory. He started to appear and disappear, moving seamlessly from one room to appear to his wife in another. His wife would attempt to follow or talk to him, and he would again vanish. When she’d find him in a completely other room, he’d say he had been there the entire time. Local police officers were called out to the farm, and they witnessed this phenomenon as well. Finally, famed paranormal investigators, Ed and Lorraine Warren, were sent for to help. They turned to Bishop Robert McKenna, asking the bishop to perform an exorcism. The exorcism was performed, and Ed Warren nearly died in the process. But in the end, it was deemed a success. Things didn’t end on a positive note for Frenchy, however. On a completely different charge, he was later arrested for sexually abusing a minor. #11 The Glasgow Poltergeist This paranormal activity was witnessed by police as recently as August of this year, 2016. On August 8th and 9th, the police in Glasgow, Scotland were called to a house in Rutherglen. Once they arrived, they witnessed flickering lights, flying clothes, an oven that opened and closed on its own, and a lampshade placed upside down. Even more curious, a Chihuahua that was running around the garden suddenly flew up atop a 7 foot hedge. No evidence of criminality was found. The family of the property was in a complete panic when officers arrived. The paranormal activity lasted for two days and was witnessed by Police Scotland on both. The family went to stay with relatives during this episode, and a Catholic priest was called in to bless the house. The incidents were not easy to explain away. In fact, the officers on the call had anticipated a mental health issue, but when they arrived and witnessed the goings-on for themselves, they simply could not understand it. The officers then phoned their superior officers, who thought they were exaggerating, but the incident was put on ‘active inquiry.’ The police also turned to social services and doctors to provide the house’s inhabitants support. Demonologist, Jason Love, believes the paranormal poltergeist may have been thriving off of the energy of young teens in the house. #10 The Hung Military Man Have you ever seen the ghost of a suicide victim? Well, a young man, tripping on drugs, did. A first-hand account from a police officer involved a delusional 20-year-old and a military uniform. The officer received a “5150,” which is a call to a home for a mental evaluation. When he arrived, the owner of the home, a woman around 50 years old, said that her young son had been doing drugs and was hallucinating that an old man had hung himself in his room. She told the police that she was afraid to go into her son’s room herself, because she feared that one of his drug addict friends had hung himself. The police officer went to speak to her son, who was on a stimulant of some kind. The young man said that a female spirit told him not to go into his bedroom, because her father had hung himself in there, attired in his “Class A” military uniform. The officer then went and checked out the room, only to find no body hanging there. He was informing the mother and consoling her, when a veteran police officer arrived to help assist. The veteran officer took the first officer aside and told him that he’d responded to this residence earlier in his career. An older male had hung himself in that very bedroom. The veteran officer couldn’t remember any further details. The first officer searched in the patrol car’s report management system and found that the man who’d committed suicide was a World War II veteran. He’d been wearing his military uniform when he killed himself. #9 The Station Ghost Officers often spend long hours watching surveillance video at their stations. And that’s just what Officer Karl Romero was doing on a Saturday night in 2014 at the Espanola police station in New Mexico. Everything was quiet. Calm. Peaceful. Until he spied an odd visual on the entryway cameras, directed at the station. At first, Romero suspected the hazy white figure he noticed on the video was a bug. Until he saw that this “bug” had legs. He blinked and looked closer. The figure was bright and white, like a ghost. Romero knew the figure wasn’t a random living, breathing person, because the police station had a gate securing it, along with an alarm system. He relayed this information to his superiors the following day. Surprisingly, many introduced their own uncanny stories into the mix. Some said they’d spotted strange visuals in the lobby, and others had heard creepy noises in the station, which they couldn’t uncover. Romero reiterated his experience to KOAT TV. He believes in ghosts and believes the figure is somehow related to a string of unsolved murders in the area over the years. #8 The “Demon House” If you joke around about your children being “possessed,” think again. The “Demon House” in Gary, Indiana put true evil in the children that lived there. Latoya Ammons and Rosa Campbell – the mother and grandmother, respectively, of three children – said that the Ammons’ children were possessed be dark entities that forced them to walk up walls backward and levitate in midair. Unexplainable footprints had also appeared throughout the home. It wasn’t until a photograph was taken, with a “figure” standing in the window of the home’s porch that local police got involved. The photograph was passed around the police department, alongside a note that claimed no one was in the house when the photo was taken. However, though the picture was later proven to be a hoax, produced via an app, many people still believed the house was haunted, even priests, social workers, and Police Captain Charles Austin, who paid witness to the 2014 paranormal events that occurred in the Demon House. He stated that he believed the house truly held something evil. He told journalists he thought Ammons was lying at first, but once he’d visited her home, he was “a believer.” The Department of Child Services was called in, as was a registered nurse, to assess the children. The case manager, Valerie Washington, and the nurse, Willie Lee Walker, both claimed they’d witnessed the 9-year-old boy walk backwards up the wall to the ceiling before landing on the floor on his feet. Washington said the boy had a “weird grin” on his face. Washington also heard the 7-year-old speak in a demonic voice. He bore his teeth and growled. His eyes then rolled into the back of his head before he passed out. It was time to call in those with an eye for demons. The house was investigated by psychics, who determined that more than 200 demons haunted this house, and they were possessing the Ammons’ children. When the children were possessed, their voices deepened, eerie smiles crept across their lips, and their eyes started to bulge from their sockets. The Ammon family doctor didn’t believe in this possession nonsense, and stated that their mother was inciting the children to display this crazy behavior, all to gain attention. The Ammons’ children were taken from their mother for a time, but the family has since been brought back together. No further paranormal events have been reported by the family. Zak Bagans, the executive producer of Ghost Adventures, purchased the house and, in early 2016, the “Demon House” was demolished. #7 The Devil Possesses Don Decker Don Decker was imprisoned for receiving stolen property and, in 1983, he was provided compassionate leave in order to attend his grandpa’s funeral. During his leave, he stayed with friends of his family in Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania. He was upstairs washing his hands in a bathroom, when he suddenly grew dizzy and collapsed on the ground. Once he returned to consciousness, he headed downstairs, where Bob Kieffer inquired about some deep scratch marks on his wrist. Decker replied that he’d collapsed and had a vision of an elderly man whose head was adorned with a crown. A few moments later, dripping water leaked from the walls and ceiling of the house. Kieffer assumed a pipe had burst, so he called his landlord to report the leak. But they then realized that the pipes weren’t broken and were positioned on the opposite side of the house. The water started to fall more heavily, like raindrops, and it even began soaking up from the floor. Kieffer and another male guest looked at Decker, who appeared to be in a trance. Shortly later, they phoned the police. But this mystery didn’t end with rainfall. Once they got off the phone, Decker began levitating from the floor, and his body was launched across the room, slamming into walls, and producing new scratches all over him. When police officers, Richard Wolbert and John Baujan, arrived on the scene, they were torn. Wolbert thought it was a hoax, while Baujan trusted in the paranormal. Wolbert decided not to file a report, but the following day, two new officers chose to go investigate the paranormal event for themselves. John Rundle and William Davies later reported that they’d seen Decker’s skin burning from a gold cross he wore. They also witnessed the levitation as Decker was flung around the room again. Shortly later, Decker returned to prison. Some of the prison’s duty officers claim to have seen drips of water moving upwards on Decker’s cell walls. When a plumber was called to fix this, the man grew disturbed after investigating Decker’s cell and left straight away. Many of the prison’s officers believe that the prisoner had become possessed by the devil and was endowed with paranormal powers. #6 The Call Is Coming from Inside the House A call was made to the police in St. Louis on November 28, 2006. Officer Sean Haefeli answered the call, heading over to investigate a family at the 200 block of Runyon Avenue who hadn’t been seen in days. Haefeli was shot by one of the residents of the home, Tony Lynn. Lynn then faced a five-hour standoff with police and was eventually shot and killed by a police sniper. What the police failed to find during the first inspection of the residence was the bodies of Tony Lynn’s grandmother and two of his siblings. They were found by relatives of the Lynns’ three days later. Several months later, Haefeli was back on the field after recovering from his wounds. He was told by other officers that they’d received a number of 911 calls from the Lynn residence, despite the fact that the phone was disconnected. Each time, the caller would hang up. Haefeli decided to investigate this oddity for himself. When he arrived back at the Lynn residence, his skin started to crawl. The electricity had been shut off, the windows boarded up, and four crosses – representing the four that were killed on site – had been planted in the lawn. “It looked like a house from Nightmare on Elm Street,” Haefeli said. He didn’t go into the home that day. But a few days later, he bucked up the courage to investigate. It was late in the evening when Haefeli entered with his flashlight. He said this is when “things got weird.” He noticed a Ouija board was set out, and the marker had landed over the letter U. Haefeli felt a sharp intake of breath, saying, “It was like it was pointing to me.” The stench of tear gas lingered in the basement. A bar was set with wine glasses. Haefeli walked slowly across the room, nearing the closet where they’d found the bodies. A frigid breath of air rushed past him, sending shivers up his spine. “It made the hairs on my neck and arms stand up,” he recalled. “I said what I wanted to say to the victims and then just ran out of there. It felt like something was constricting me. I felt like somebody was there watching me the whole time.” Interestingly enough, after Haefeli’s visit to the home, the 911 calls ceased, as if Lynn’s victims had been waiting for him to say a final goodbye. #5 A Police Captain Investigates His Past Life Robert Snow, a retired Indianapolis police department captain, was placed on a paranormal case involving past lives. Snow was the commander of the homicide branch and, at first, he was skeptical about the supernatural elements of this case. Snow didn’t believe in this nonsense. Reincarnation, past lives – it all sounded absurd to him. But he did find the concept interesting, and he opened his mind enough to investigate. He even began reading a book on past life regression hypnosis. He decided to try it out for himself. During his hypnosis, he described in great detail the history of an unrenowned painter, named Carroll Beckwith. While he was under, he even saw quite clearly one of the works of this painter. He wrote in his book, Looking for Carroll Beckwith: “The evidence I uncovered in this two-year investigation is so overwhelming that if it had been a criminal case, there would be no plea bargaining. A conviction would be assured.” As he continued to delve into the paranormal and investigate what he’d discovered during his regression hypnosis sessions, he came face-to-face with one of the two paintings his visions had produced so vividly to him while on vacation. The spontaneous viewing in a tiny art gallery of this piece by Carroll Beckwith astounded him. He began to correlate the painter’s life with that of what he’d expressed in his hypnoses. Beckwith had kept a daily diary during his final 46 years of life that numbered more than 15,000 pages, so this served as a source of data to check the facts. He found that nearly all the information he’d provided during the hypnosis proved true to life. In the end, the skeptical man became a believer. #4 Capitol Theatre Haunting Salt Lake City’s Capitol Theatre is haunted. That’s what many people who’ve worked in the building claim. Haunted by what? Ghouls. Goblins. Dark forces. Perhaps a long-deceased teenage usher, crying out for some attention. Salt Lake County sheriff’s deputy, Dave Murphy, suggested the theatre was haunted by a “load of crap”…that is, until he, himself, saw dark shadows reverberating through the theatre walls. Murphy was a security guard for the building and spent nights alone by himself in the haunted theatre. He heard doors bang shut, leaving the windows vibrating, and even saw a ghostly woman clothed in early 20th century garb. “She walked right past me, as I sat in the control room,” Murphy claimed. “My jaw dropped.” A Syfy episode of “Paranormal Witness” recounts Murphy’s claims, as well as those from theatre staff and police officers. Mark Lewis, the show’s producer, said that they look for credible sources, like law enforcement witnesses, as opposed to random head-cases. Along with three police officer interviewees, Blair Fuller, the administrative manager of the Salt Lake County Center for the Arts, was also asked to speak on the haunting. He said he’d first witnessed paranormal activity in the building around 1997, when he was working at night in the theatre and discovered the elevator was operating by itself, while file doors flew open and then were forcefully flung closed. Fuller said he never felt uncomfortable with the activity. “In my experience,” he said, “it’s almost like a teenager trying to get some attention. And once you acknowledge that, it stops.” In fact, a fire broke out in the theatre back in 1947, killing a 17-year-old usher. This is who some suspect to be haunting the theatre. Others were made uncomfortable by the paranormal encounters, however. Murphy suggested, “Toward the end, they wanted me out of that building for whatever reason.” He claims the black shadows he saw permeating throughout the building once “attacked” him. “It felt just like I got a punch in the chest. Literally, I could not talk. Whatever it was, it had the power to shut me up." And still more credible sources have also claimed to have met with supernatural activity within the building. Some have said the men’s room is particularly haunted, as are the basement and the elevators. Murphy recalls his days working in the theatre. “Some nights I would be shaking so bad, it would take me hours before I would unwind. A lot of people think I’m crazy, but I know what I saw." #3 Evil Resides in Enfield Enfield was rarely ever newsworthy, but when an evil entity rolled into town in 1977, the story hit the papers. The owner of the haunted home in question, Peggy Hodgson, said that a dark force had entered her home, causing her sons’ beds to shake uncontrollably. This paranormal activity was first reported to her by her daughter, Janet, after which Peggy was on high alert. The following evening, a loud bang exploded from her children’s bedroom. She flew to the room and found a chest of drawers shaking uncontrollably. She tried to move it back in place with the help of her children, but it wouldn’t budge. Throughout the house, a bizarre knocking sound could be heard. Not only that, but Janet started to levitate over her bed. Most people in town were skeptical about this story, believing Peggy and her children were fabricating the entire thing. But Ed and Lorraine Warren, two famous paranormal investigators, came to take a look, as did Police Officer Carolyn Heeps, who confirmed that she’d witnessed paranormal activity by signing an affidavit after she’d been called to the house. What did she witness? She saw a chair levitating above the floor and flying about 4 feet across the room. The police left the Hodgson’s home, stating that they couldn’t help the family, as no law had been broken. Although no one can prove this event true, the levitating chair reached fame. It was featured in the horror movie, The Conjuring 2. #2 The Ghostly Reporter The sheriff of a small New Mexico town had to eat his words when he was met with this paranormal event. The town news was covered by a local reporter, Bob D., who would listen to the police scanner to find the action. Whether it was fires, terrible car crashes, homicides, or any other major event, Bob was there. Everyone on the police force was familiar with Bob and liked him, as he always showed up at the scene and was a bit of a jokester. He would stand behind people and flick their ears and, when they batted the imaginary insect away, they’d turn around to find it was just Bob, the joker. But Bob was to meet an unfunny end when he died fairly quickly from lung cancer. Although he wanted to be cremated, his wife had him buried. After his funeral, a number of folks claimed to have seen Bob at crime scenes. In fact, more than 20 reports from both police officers and civilians, alike, were made, detailing these visions of Bob. However, the straight-laced sheriff of this small town remained skeptical. But one night, he showed up with his wife at a relative’s house, pale as a ghost and with his gun drawn. After calming down, he explained what he’d just experienced. The sheriff and his wife were at home on the couch, watching TV, when the sheriff felt an itch on his ear. He scratched it repeatedly until his wife asked him what was wrong. The sheriff turned around and saw their bedroom door open. Who was standing in the doorway, but Bob D., himself. The sheriff launched to his feet, swore, hollered at his wife, and she turned to see Bob smile at the pair. He made eye contact with each of them and crossed the living room, leaving out their front door and shutting the door behind him. The sheriff raced to the door with his gun drawn, but Bob had vanished. Bob D. continued to show up to police scenes for another 2-3 months, and the sheriff saw him on two additional occasions. Never again did he denounce the paranormal. #1 Silbury Hill Sighting Tall beings. A formation. A crop inspection. Paranormal activity from extraterrestrial beings was witnessed by an unnamed off-duty police officer near a crop circle at Silbury Hill in July, 2009. At first, the officer in question thought these beings were forensic scientists, as they were dressed all in white and seemed to be examining the area. But then he saw they were all identical, with blond hair and standing more than 6 feet tall. He also felt some surge of static electricity throughout the field. It was then that he knew this wasn’t normal. The officer claimed that one of these beings stood at the edge of the hill, another stood several yards further along the tramline, and yet another stood halfway down the hill. The officer said he “knew” they were inspecting the crop and, when asked how he knew, he replied, “You know what day of the week it is, but no one has told you. You haven’t seen a calendar, you just know.” Andrew Russell and Colin Andrews, two crop circle researchers, investigated this incident. As they spoke to the officer, they began to wonder if he had an unknown psychic awareness. The officer said that the figures began to race away at top speed, as though he were watching “fast-forward mode” on a videotape. They raced away and then vanished. During the interview, the hairs stood up on the officer’s arms, as he told the tale and relived it. Russell, who is also a clinical hypnotherapist, ran through the experience with the officer a number of times. He even drove and timed the route. According to Russell, there is a discrepancy of five minutes between the time accounted for by the officer and the actual time it took to run the route. Following the event, the officer was confronted with several “poltergeist experiences.” Knocks were heard at his front door, but no one would be there when he answered. Electrical items began to break down. And, even worse, the officer felt a strange presence in his home. When he would turn a corner from his kitchen, he’d see a sudden flash of an 8-foot black figure looming in front of him. The officer began to have flashes of “knowing.” He understood that the figures had been clone-like, identical, and with a common intelligence. He doesn’t believe they created the crop circle, but he does believe that the beings communicated to him that he shouldn’t have witnessed this event. The officer has no idea where these ideas generate from; he just feels they are absolute truth. The officer also noticed a strange orange globe in the sky above his house. He awoke from sleep one night and went outside to smoke a cigarette when he spotted this strange floating orb hanging above, a few hundred yards from his garden. Like the beings, the globe stayed for a bit, hovering and swaying back and forth, before shooting off at lightning speed. To this day, these paranormal events remain a mystery.

奧克蘭在太平洋的最西南面。 這裡有大約 150 萬人口，是紐西蘭人口最多的城市。 奧克蘭是遊覽風景秀麗的海岸線 和探索北島各個隱藏洞穴的理想基地。 這裡又稱為帆船之都， 擁有船隻的人均比例冠絕全球。 這個城市位於兩大天然港灣之間，很容易就去到海邊。 奧克蘭最大的地標是朗伊托托島， 在市內的所有地方均觸目可見。 奧克蘭作為全國最大的城市，擁有現代化的商場、 寬敞的城市公園和大量的文化景點。 到古老的文藝復興風格倉庫艾略特‧司寶斯享用早餐， 再沿附近的皇后街購物區漫步。 然後出發探索市內主要景點。 在中央商業區外，參觀奧克蘭 最時尚的龐森比路上的時髦商店和餐廳。 沿著密遜灣的海濱長廊漫步，享受市內海灘的美景。 奧克蘭海濱最有特色的建築 是愛德華風格的渡輪碼頭。 到對岸的達文港享用海鮮午餐。 您可以花幾天時間探索奧克蘭國際化的街道和海灣， 但最吸引的景點是在市區範圍之外： 就是未受污染的大自然！ 奧克蘭崎嶇的海岸線上的陡峭懸崖 和連綿起伏的山丘景色非常壯觀。 駕車到懷塔克雷山脈的原始熱帶雨林 享受樹梢漫步，觀賞更多紐西蘭特色動植物。 這個地區公園位於奧克蘭西部。 公園附近，沿著北島的西部火山海岸線有皮哈海灘、 獅子岩一直伸延到北部。很多經驗豐富的滑浪好手都來這裡一展身手。 無論您選擇哪一個西岸海灘，景色同樣令人嘆為觀止， 這裡是堆沙堡壘、釣魚、划船和漫步沙灘的理想地點。 回到市區，可以到奧克蘭中央公園參觀， 這裡是主要的公共公園，當地人會在這裡打板球。 來這裡享受一下悠閒的生活， 正是這個偏遠島國上普遍的生活方式。 來到莊嚴的奧克蘭戰爭紀念館， 聽聽故事，看看奧特亞羅瓦金寶藏， 毛利人土著稱紐西蘭為「長白雲之鄉」。 他們的祖先在大約一千年前航行到這裡， 而他們深感自豪的文化仍然活靈活現。 孩子們一定會喜歡奧克蘭動物園， 他們可以看看和親親非洲大草原的動物。 「彩虹盡頭」是另一個好去處。 玩刺激的機動遊戲，和朋友互相碰撞。 在空中旋轉 ，又或者急速下降！ 市中心的天空塔還有更多刺激的活動， 在這裡您可以玩極速的高飛跳。 如果您只想看看風景，可乘電梯到觀景平台， 往下看看奧克蘭市中心的街道。 日落前，步行或駕車前往伊甸山頂， 在這個位於市內的火山， 欣賞閃爍燈光，以及市內最宏偉的建築。 奧克蘭擁有無窮資源， 毛利人遠在多個世紀前經已發現。 他們稱這裡為 Tāmaki Makaurau，意思是「一百人的渴求之地」。 這裡的吸引力仍然存在，加上獨特的歷史、 未被開發的大自然、合家歡景點和隨和的生活方式， 使這裡成為每年數以百萬海外遊客的心怡目的地。 Nau mai Tāmaki Makaurau! - 歡迎遊覽奧克蘭！

#15 Our list begins with Xenia Ignatyeva, who took a selfie while standing on a bridge 28 feet off the ground. Why? Well, what’s the most important reason to take a selfie in the first place? You already know the answer, to impress her friends. What else? The 17-year-old Russian girl at one moment suddenly lost her balance and fell on a cable. The most disturbing part of this tragedy is that the cable literally electrocuted her. All what was left was a photo of a smiling girl, who had an entire life waiting for her, before she’d decided to take her last selfie. #14 Jojo Tsai was a pretty 20-year-old Chinese girl, who took a selfie at the very top of a tall building. She was able to upload it to her Instagram profile only a couple of minutes before throwing herself over the building’s edge. Again, we have to ask why? What could be the reason to end a young life in such a tragic way? According to unofficial sources and numerous social media postings it turns out that a heartbreaking split from her boyfriend was the emotional “trigger” behind it. In one of her last postings she wrote, “I never thought that you would deceive me, but I still can’t stop loving you. After I’m dead, I will haunt you day and night. I will never be apart from you again.” We can’t tell for sure, if her ex-boyfriend keeps her last photo with him all the time. In addition, if you hear a scary story about a ghost-girl from China don’t be surprised. It seems that we’re witnessing the major change of “rules”. Not so long ago, the tragic souls, who decided to end their current miseries by killing themselves, used to leave suicide notes. Now, some leave a selfie. #13 There is nothing wrong about making a decision to take a selfie on an airplane. Right? Who doesn’t like to take selfies while traveling? Right again? However, there’s something spooky and disturbingly diabolical about what happened next after this famously infamous selfie was taken. These two were among the tragically killed victims of Malaysian Airlines notorious flight MH 17. As we all know this plane was shot down while flying through the Ukranian airspace by a missile. In a strange way, this picture has become a recognizable symbol, and with no exaggeration, a true synonym for this plane’s tragedy. #12 Sylwia Rajchel was an ordinary 23-year-old girl, with a strong desire to take selfies in unusual places and under extraordinary circumstances. This time, Sylwia a Polish medical student decided for her newest, and unfortunately last selfie to include stunning images of an eye-catching bridge. While taking the selfie, she fell from a 15 feet bridge. This poor girl was visiting Seville, Spain. As expected, she just couldn’t resist paying a visit to the famous Puente de Triana bridge. This is the place where she stopped to take this photo. She was actually balancing on the ledge when she fell to her sudden and tragic death. #11 On April 26, 2014 a young and cheerful Courtney Sanford posted her picture while singing to the extremely popular Pharrel Williams song 'Happy'. The trouble was, she did that while driving through North Carolina in her car. A couple of seconds later she crashed her car into a truck. This tragic accident proved to be fatal for her. To this very day, it’s remained unknown what the reason was for her to lose control while driving. Yet, we’re pretty much convinced that she was more concerned about her selfie, than her safety. The moral of this story just couldn’t be more obvious, could it? Don’t drink and drive, we all know that. Yet, there’s an additional rule we have to include, as well. Don’t drive, sing songs and take selfies all at the same. #10 Meet Collette Moreno and Ashley Theobald. These two were on their way to Collette’s bachelorette party, which took place in Kansas City, Missouri. They thought, it would be a great idea to snap this selfie. However, not too long after the well-known shot was taken, a pick-up truck hit the Chevy Malibu that they were in with the destructive force. Allegedly, the driver lost control of his car, because a passing car emitted a lot of fumes, causing him to have a sudden asthma attack. This is really a disturbing incident, which gives you no choice than to think a lot about your actions while driving. #09 This selfie was snapped by a famous Puerto Rican artist and musician called Jadiel. He was able to upload this recognizable selfie to his Instagram account only a couple of moments before he suffered a fatal motorcycle crash in New York in 2014. It’s definitely worth mentioning that this selfie has nothing to do with Jadiel’s tragic death. However, we just can’t stop asking ourselves, is taking a selfie right before you start a journey a bad omen of some kind? It just like we’re sending an invitation to dark, brutal and deadly forces to pay us a visit and make sure it’s the last picture we ever take. #08 Jenni Rivera was a famous 43-year-old singer and songwriter in Latin America. In this photo we can see her posing for a selfie, which turned out to be her last one. She was traveling with friends after attending a show. Very briefly after they took this selfie the plane crash claimed their young lives. It was a private Learjet, which flew specially for this occasion. Unfortunately, all seven people on board quickly died. The crash provided almost no chances for survival, because the plane was nose-diving at more than 700mph at one point. Undoubtedly, this was an unusually violent incident even for the most extreme plane crashes. #07 In 2014 there was a disturbing report about an 18-year-old named Kelene Guiterrez, who tragically died after attempting to make a selfie while hanging from a door insider her bathroom. Yes, you heard that right. The story goes that this teen was a huge fan of taking selfies in unusual and quite outrageous places. This also includes a bathroom door of all the places in the world she could’ve chosen. Allegedly, she posed on a door, fell, and violently struck her head on the toilet. The head injury caused her death, because of the angle and the devastating force of the blow itself. You don’t have to worry, there’s no way you can experience the same, if you happen to slip in your own bathroom. However, this poor girl was challenging her bad luck in the worst possible way. #06 Our next story about deadly selfies includes a 21-year-old guy named Oscar Otero Aguilar, who lost his life when he allegedly tried to take a selfie with nothing less than a gun. He was eager to take a picture with this gun for his Facebook profile in July of 2014. This Mexican gun lover accidentally shot himself in the head while taking the picture, and sadly didn't survive. This story really sounds like any selfie enthusiast worst nightmare. In one hand you’re holding your camera, while in your other hand there’s a gun. You plan to use only one of them, but the next thing you know, both things shoot. #05 On June 8th, 2014, India experienced the terrible Beas river tragedy. One of its most devastating and shocking consequences was associated with the 24 young engineering students and their local tour guide, who were washed away after a massive and sudden release of water from the Larji dam in the area of the Mandi district in India. To add to the misery for the victims’ families and friends, this selfie of the cheerful and happy-looking group was all what was left of them, before the tragedy was triggered by the giant wave of released water. What an unimaginable waste of so many young and promising lives. This is so terrible. #04 This shocking selfie death story is an illustrative example of just how dangerous things can really be in the Middle East. Mohammed Shaar and his friends were ordinary guys, who had posed for the group selfie photo, when just a couple of seconds later a car bomb, which is originally designed to kill a high-ranking local politician, killed them all instead. The incident actually took place in Beirut, Lebanon in 2012. As you can see, they were just a couple of young people enjoying each other’s company and nice weather. Who could’ve thought that this would be the very last thing they did together in their lives? #03 This story includes a 13-year-old girl with a name Karen Hernández, who actually wanted to make a selfie on the banks of the local El Tunal river in the area of Durango, Mexico. Unfortunately, she accidentally fell into the river and drowned. The firefighters were able to recover her body only a couple of days later. To this very day it wasn’t quite clear what went wrong in this situation. As you might’ve expected there were quite a few speculations and rumors circulating among the locals and Karen’s school friends. However, none of them could provide an acceptable explanation for a tragic incident, which claimed the life of this young girl. On the other side, there’s something about nature that intrigues us to take eye-catching selfies near the shores, and especially around the bridges. Do we really want people risking their lives just to take a cool picture? #02 In March 2014 a selfie photo was all that what was left of a 21-year-old man, who died in Jaén, Spain. Why this story took the #2 position on our list? Well, this poor guy really wanted to take a special selfie. This is why, he climbed on to the top of a moving train to take it. This is definitely an extreme choice, when it comes to selfies, isn’t it? Can you believe this guy was literally electrocuted, while attempting this? Where did he get this crazy idea to jump on a moving train? Maybe, it’s about time to do something about the overwhelming “selfie-mania”, which claims more and more lives all over the world. A simple picture of an average smiley face is just not good enough. Your friends and loved ones are pushing you to go further all the time. Nowadays, you really need to do some crazy thing in order to impress your friends. Even if it means to jump on a moving train. #01 Here’s our top story from the list. However, we can’t say it’s a winner. Unfortunately, there are no winners on this list. Each and any of people on this lost paid the ultimate price for his or her obsession with taking selfies. Yet, we just didn’t want to end this list in dark and depressing tones. We don’t want to leave you thinking about the disturbing and shocking fourteen deaths, which left scary reminders after them. So, how do you feel about a survival story for a change? There are two young girls, who got their rare and priceless second chance. But, let’s see what they did with it, eventually. There were two lovely and young Iranian women, who were singing along to a song while driving. Sounds familiar? So, what happened next? Well, these girls were occupied with the song on their car radio, including the additional “activity” of taking a selfie, so it was no surprise at all that all of these distractions caused them to crash. Luckily, both of them survived. Now, the most logical thing for you to think is that these lucky girls learned their lesson. Oh boy, you’re so wrong. They’re obviously helpless selfie-addicts. Why? Well, they even posed for both an ambulance and a hospital-based selfie afterwards. Can you believe it? After all they’d gone through, they had to make one more selfie. Seriously? How crazy you had to be to do such a thing?

In shows like Kitchen Nightmares, Hotel Hell, and Hell’s Kitchen, the chef had to eat some terrible meals. While most of the time Ramsay managed to keep down his food, sometimes it just wasn’t possible. Because we are all lovers of Gordon at his most expressive, we tracked down another top 10 times when Gordon Ramsay dramatically spat out food! Nasty Gravy The Prohibition Grille was a once-in-a-lifetime kind of restaurant. It seemed like it had all the perfect ingredients to make the best Kitchen Nightmares stew. The owner was completely clueless. Plus, she also belly-danced during dinner - a move that confused customers and made Gordon want to hide out of utter embarrassment. But it all went down when people complained about the gravy. First, Ramsay had the owner taste it. Then, Gordon was curious himself. When Ramsay took a spoonful, he couldn’t even swallow it. After that, the chef ordered that all plates with gravy had to be sent back immediately. This also prompted Gordon to further inspect the kitchen. All in all, the kitchen was not only a mess, it was a health risk. But before we show you more of Gordon’s misadventures, show us some love! Hit that subscribe button and don’t miss out on more BabbleTop videos. Now, back to Gordon’s dramatics... Praying over the Chitlins Chef Shelley thought everything she did was close to perfection, while everyone around her disagreed. Ramsay had his usual sample meal, and things didn’t start very well. Which is basically like committing a sin when it comes to a soul food restaurant. The collard greens weren’t much better. Nothing was making Ramsay happy. But things were going to get even worse. In fact, Gordon was so withdrawn about eating the food that he even decided to pray. Praying, though, didn't help much. It even sent shivers down Ramsay’s spine. Maybe too literally, as he rushed to the bathroom. Takeout Room Service When Gordon arrived at the Keating Hotel, he knew it was going to be trouble. The main lobby had more red than those elevators in The Shining. Every floor of this hotel had a different model car on display. The room itself looked really empty. Plus, it had a jacuzzi tub right in the middle of the room. Gordon was absolutely losing it. His only hope? That the room service would make up for all the weirdness around him. Well, it didn’t. The soup was barely even there Gordon actually poured it into a cup - and it didn’t even fill it all the way! The chicken slider? The barbecue pizza? Gordon didn’t even have the courage to take a bite. At least Gordon found a good use for the container. Troubled Dinner Service The Classic American was in a tough spot. The customers were getting restless and were completely unsatisfied. The waitress and the kitchen staff were fighting. Things didn’t get better when the food finally started going out, though. Every customer seemed baffled by their meals. When someone complained about a sandwich with too much sauce, Gordon decided to taste it. Don’t people learn? Ramsay took a bite out of the sandwich and then promptly threw it out in the trash. Can it even get more dramatic than that? But Gordon had enough when he spotted a horrible plate of vegetables coming out of the kitchen. He actually had everyone on the staff stop and gather around him. He even had them touching it, to show how horrible was the consistency of that plate was. Microwaved Crepe Kitchen Nightmares was probably a hard show to endure for Gordon. But the worst part for Gordon, probably, was having to eat at those bad restaurants. Take what happened with La Frite, for example. First, Gordon ordered the La Frite salad. None of it looked good, though. Turns out, it was a known complaint. Martin, like many chefs before him, didn’t see anything wrong with the food. After the failed salad, it was time for the seafood crepe. That puzzled Gordon - why call it a crepe at all? The dish itself looked horrible. It also tasted horrendous. Gordon said it was hideous. Apparently, chef Martin didn’t care about the food anymore. When the quiche arrived, Ramsay was certain that it had been microwaved. Didn’t he know he was being recorded? Eventually, he caved in and admitted he microwaved the food. Chewy Octopus When Ramsay arrived at Guiseppi’s, things didn’t look good. Chef Sam and his father, Joe, were already bickering even before Ramsay ordered anything. Sam didn’t even have the usual bravado most chefs in Kitchen Nightmares do. The salad arrived quickly on Gordon’s table. Too bad that it didn't taste good at all. Meanwhile, the father and son duo were still bickering back in the kitchen. When the waitress brought another plate, Ramsay still couldn’t stop thinking about the octopus. Gordon even gave a piece to the waitress, so she could try it herself. Suffice to say, she didn’t look that excited to try it. Mind you, that was just the first dish out of many that Gordon had to eat. The rest of the meal didn’t fare much better. Bacon and Chocolate Gordon sat down at the Keating's restaurant to sample some of their meals. Right away, things looked messy. The kitchen had another case of the chef actually not caring anymore about their food. You could see it in Chef Brian's eyes. As expected, Gordon wasn’t a fan of any of the food. But it was the dessert that left Gordon speechless. A lot of people like bacon. A lot of people like chocolate. But mixing these two together sounds like a recipe for disaster. When the pizza arrived, Gordon had enough. That wasn’t his only critique, however. The manager just looked aghast. Gordon took a bite, while some people looked on. They probably expected a big reaction out of Gordon. Which he provided. Sushi Pizza What even is a sushi pizza? Is it more like sushi or more like pizza? You could see that this order was motivated only by Gordon’s morbid curiosity. The rest of his orders were regular for a Japanese restaurant: miso soup, sashimi… plus, something called a green tower. First came the miso soup. Next up was the green tower which was too "grey" - you might say. Then, the sashimi was frozen, though the waitress didn’t know it. Then, came the main course. The star of this whole thing. Gordon took a bite out of it. You should give him props for that alone! But courage doesn’t do much when you’re talking about the sushi pizza. He even covered the plate with a napkin probably because he couldn’t bear staring at it much longer. The Infamous Gumbo For the first episode of Hell’s Kitchen, all the chefs in the competition must prepare their signature dish for Gordon. Some might leave the chef impressed - while others will get their first taste of being savagely critiqued by Gordon. The latter was what happened with Antonia. Antonia, on the other hand, seemed sure her gumbo was going to be a success. Maybe she makes a better version of it at home? Gordon, then, had the difficult task of actually eating a little bit of the gumbo. It was his job, after all. That’s when Antonia realized she was in trouble. Gordon, then, went back to the trash can again. The food was so bad, Gordon had to share it. Ramsay passed it around and forced everyone to eat it. Bad Scallops During the first episode of the UK version of Kitchen Nightmares, Gordon had his very first encounter with poorly made food. It was the restaurant Bonapartes. Business was struggling, with sometimes only two customers per night. When Gordon observed a dinner service, he saw how inexperienced the kitchen staff were. Gordon was expecting that the chef’s true potential would be put on display. Ramsay was expecting something truly memorable, that belonged on a fine dining menu. Oh, it was memorable all right! 從意大利首都羅馬開車往西北只需數小時， 在亞平寧山腳下，是如詩歌般優美的佛羅倫斯。 這座華麗的地中海城市四處皆是歷史建築， 絕對是歐遊的必到之地。 歡迎來到但丁、馬基雅維利 (Machiavelli ) 和米高安哲羅 (Michelangelo ) 的誔生地， 達文西亦曾在這裡學習繪畫。 佛羅倫斯歡迎您！ 佛羅倫斯的歷史要追溯到公元前 59 年， 凱撒大帝曾在阿諾河畔紮營。 這座精緻的古城 以早期羅馬為基礎而建， 並且以購買皮革涼鞋和皮包而著名。 想要祈求好運的話，就把一枚硬幣放到「小豬」的鼻子上吧！ 雖然它只是個複製品，但誰知道它會不會靈驗呢！ 在羅馬人首次聚居於此的 1,400 年後， 教會和富商家庭統治了佛羅倫斯。 麥迪奇家族在此興建了許多宏偉的建築， 展現精心設計的藝術特色。 他們精心挑選繪畫大師、建築師和雕刻家， 建造了歐洲其中一個最具文化氣息的城市。 聖羅倫佐教堂便是最能代表其貢獻的例子， 教堂由菲利波布魯內萊斯基 (Filippo Brunelleschi) 設計， 是意大利文藝復興建築風格的最好例子。 菲利波同時興建了座落在主教座堂廣場上的 聖母百花大教堂的圓頂，這座教堂已有 750 年歷史。 喜愛宗教藝術的同好絕不能錯過烏菲茲美術館， 美術館橫跨了 舊皇宮至阿諾河之間幾條街。 即使在戶外也能隨處可見許多雕像， 例如在教堂、噴泉和廣場。 由米高安哲羅雕刻的偉人大衛像 是世界數一數二的著名雕像之一。 領主廣場上的大衛像是複製品， 真品則完好保存在廣場北面的 學院畫廊中。 您可以穿越有 400·年歷史的舊橋， 正因為舊橋太美，所以在二次大戰時免於受炸毀之劫。 橋的彼岸是碧堤宮， 這裡曾是麥迪奇家族的府邸， 在這處廣大的公眾藝廊收藏了家族一些家傳之寶。 在佛羅倫斯，每處都有令人 忙著舉起相機拍照的景色， 例如那些壯麗宏偉的建築物。 怪不得佛羅倫斯 俘獲了那麼多遊客的心。 準備向佛羅倫斯說再見吧， 在離開之前記得回頭再看一眼阿諾河， 這條孕育出文興復興的河流。

10 Things That Would Happen if Minimum Wage Went to $15 Everywhere 10. The Rise of the Machines Forget Terminator. Forget The Matrix. The real cause of the machine revolution lies not in military programs, but in the battle for a higher minimum wage. According to The Economist, there’s only one likely outcome to a yuge minimum wage hike: mass automation. Right now, machines and computers are capable of doing a heck of a lot that low-skilled humans can, such as driving trucks and manning checkouts. The reason that they don’t isn’t due to some fancy-pants robot-workers’ union, but because they simply cost too much. It’s way more cost-effective for an employer to keep you working at the checkout for $7.50 an hour than it is for them to buy a machine to do your job, so they don’t. But when that $15 wage hike comes in, suddenly the robots are looking a lot more attractive. The outcome? Jobs will disappear faster than you can say “Skynet.” Nationally, millions would be out of work. Globally, billions. That would mean completely restructuring our economies to deal with permanent mass-unemployment; a shift which wouldn’t come easy. 9. The Poor Would Still be Poor It’s important to note that robots still suck at certain jobs. Cleaning, for example, is better being done by humans. Mass-automation wouldn’t really affect such sectors. So that means a minimum wage hike would still lift some out of poverty, right? Sure. But far, far fewer than you’d think. Most supporters of the $15 minimum want to reduce poverty. But the minimum wage rarely affects those who are truly poor. Only 12.7% of US minimum wage workers come from poor households. Just under half are secondary-income earners from households with earnings three times higher than the poverty line. In other words, they’re teenagers starting their first job, or parents who took time out for raising kids and now want a bit of part-time work to fill the empty hours. The result would be a boost to these people’s finances, for sure. But the vast majority of American poor either already make $15 but don’t get enough hours, or simply don’t work at all. A mass-applied $15 minimum wouldn’t affect this cohort one bit. 8. Mass Migration In the 1980s, well-meaning legislators accidentally screwed-over Puerto Rico. As a US Territory, the island became subject to the US Minimum Wage. Hooray for Puerto Rico, huh? Not so fast. The knock-on effect of this wage increase was to drive a huge chunk of the island’s residents to migrate to mainland USA. This sounds counter-intuitive, but it makes perfect sense. Puerto Rico is poor. There was simply no way employers could afford the mainland minimum wage. With automation in 1983 being a pipedream, they simply laid off workers and sent unemployment skyrocketing. Something similar would happen with a global minimum wage. Rich cities and countries that could afford the $15 hit would suddenly become Meccas for those from poor areas which couldn’t afford it. The jobless poor would flood in from territories and rural areas that couldn’t pay, leading to perhaps the greatest wave of human migration in history. And as we all know, mass-migration doesn’t always go completely smoothly… 7. Rampant Xenophobia During the Great Depression, hundreds of thousands of Americans were forced to leave Dustbowl States to look for work. Oklahoma alone lost nearly half a million of its population to more-prosperous states like California. How did the residents of richer states react to this sudden influx of poor, depressed and unemployed people? They freakin’ hated their guts. Okies were the subject of extreme discrimination from locals who thought they were stealing jobs, bringing crime, undercutting wages and just generally stinking up Sunny California with their Okie ways. Never mind that most of the Okies were family folk who just wanted to do some honest work and contribute to California, they were still hugely unpopular. It’s not hard to imagine something similar happening if a $15 minimum wage drove people from poor, rural areas into rich, urban ones. On a national scale, it would be uncomfortable. If it was global, then throw in racism and culture clash and you’re potentially sitting on a powder keg. 6. Poor Countries Would Become Poorer Everyone reading this can probably agree that paying Bangladeshi workers $0.50 per hour to toil in a sweatshop is morally ugly. Unfortunately, it’s also the way the world works. Poor countries like Bangladesh, Ethiopia and Haiti are chronically in need of investment. To ensure companies want to set up shop there, they have to offer something the West can’t. Sadly, that ‘something’ is extremely low-wage employees. Create a world where everyone from a trucker in Arizona to a garment-maker in Dhaka is worth $15 an hour, and you destroy the only competitive advantage these countries have. For a company in the US, it suddenly makes no sense at all for them to set up a factory in Asia when it costs the same as setting one up in America. So they won’t. Unless poor countries sacrifice something else in return for investment, that investment will simply dry up. Bangladeshi jobs will vanish, money will disappear, and poor countries will get even poorer. 5. The End of Outsourcing On the other hand, this would mean the end of outsourcing; a practice generally considered to be so mercenary it probably counts as one of the 7 Deadly Sins. While this is extremely bad news for those living in poorer countries, it could be pretty good for those living elsewhere. Right now, a lot of jobs that used to be done by Americans are being done abroad for a fraction of the cost. Take away those cost incentives to move abroad, and those jobs will probably stay in America (provided the government did other stuff like cut corporation tax). For those industries that can’t be automated, it could result in a glut of work available at home. It would be the same thing both Trump and Bernie Sanders like to talk about: American jobs for American workers. The downside is there are other ways countries could attract multinationals even with a global $15 minimum wage, such as low corporation tax, an unregulated market or removing certain labor restrictions. In practice, then, a global minimum wage of $15 might not end outsourcing. Instead it might trigger a race to the bottom in an entirely different area. 4. A Gigantic Small Business Crash There’s a reason campaigns like Fight for $15 stir so much moral fury. The idea that a multi-billion-dollar empire like Walmart can get away with paying its employees $7.20 per hour makes any reasonable person’s blood boil. The reality is that plenty of minimum wage employees aren’t slaving away in Walmart. They’re working for small businesses. And asking those small businesses to double their employees’ wages is like asking them to start handing out blocks of gold to all of their customers. Around a third of minimum wage employees are working at businesses that employ fewer than 50 people. Force a $15 minimum on these places, and they’re gonna go under or lay off staff or (more likely) both. That means a collapse of small businesses across the board, something that’s not exactly thrilling for stuff like innovation, the economy, or just having a few more choices of coffee place beyond Starbucks. Most of us value small businesses and independent Mom-and-Pop stores. We also value the idea of workers being paid a good minimum wage. Sadly, these two things can often be mutually-exclusive. 3. The Rise of Freelance Contract Work One of the big flaws with the minimum wage is that there are quite a few ways around it. Most of you reading this probably work in an industry that utilizes one or more of them. For example, your place might take on unpaid interns over summer. Or maybe those looking for a promotion can take part in a scheme that temporarily increases their responsibilities while not affecting their pay scale. In many industries, the ‘get around’ comes from freelance contract work. This is especially prevalent in the world of online writing which – surprise! – we happen to know a great deal about. The basic set-up is that the website will pay you per article, not per hour worked. If you’re a dashingly-handsome internet-writer with chiselled abs this isn’t a problem, as you’re capable of writing a $15 article in way under an hour. But for someone without those skills or looks… well, then you got a problem. In a world where the $15 is everywhere, plenty of companies are gonna avail themselves of freelance contracts. This means people who aren’t suited to them languishing away, taking hours and hours and hours to complete a task which will net them only paltry sums. So how about we get rid of these contracts altogether? Well, then you’re stuck with plenty of businesses going bust… and all those same workers now making nothing at all. 2. An Explosion of Spending By now, we suspect some Fight for $15 fans are more than a little upset with the direction this article has taken. Hey, thems the breaks. We just go where our research leads us. And for this entry, it has led us to a potential light at the end of this dark and mold-infested tunnel. There’s a chance a $15 minimum could spark an economy-reviving spending spree. This comes courtesy of Bloomberg, an outfit not exactly known for its leftish politics. The argument is pretty straightforward. A capitalist economy relies upon workers using their wages to buy stuff they want but don’t really need. This is the engine that drives growth. Whisk away that extra part of their paycheck marked ‘conspicuous consumption’ and the economy falters. Conversely, inflate that part wildly with a $15 minimum wage, and sit back and watch as the economy goes into overdrive. The theory is that people who earn the extra money would spend and spend like lunatics. Goods would be flying off shelves. Vacations would be booked en masse. Services would be purchased, money would go flying through the economy, and everyone would wind up being a winner. It could be a boom to rival the 2008 bust, the sort of massive boost we haven’t seen in ages. 1. Everything or Nothing At the end of all that, we have a confession to make. We don’t know what would happen if the minimum wage went to $15 everywhere. That’s not us being uninformed: literally no-one knows. While there have been plenty of studies done on minimum wage hikes, there has never been one done on a hike as enormous as the $15 one would be. It simply hasn’t happened before over a large enough area, or in enough places, for anyone to draw any firm conclusions. As a result, it’s easy to find respected economics writers claiming that a national $15 minimum would be the best thing ever; just as it’s easy to find respected writers claiming that such a hike would trigger the apocalypse. What we’ve done above is drawn on what a plurality of economists seem to think, and what theories seem to suggest, to try and draw conclusions. The reality is, no-one knows for sure what would happen applying the $15 minimum on a national scale, let alone an international one. The only certainty is that the effect would be enormous, and possibly world-changing. Whether for the better or the worse is something we’d simply have to wait to find out.

Gordon Ramsay is a cook, athlete, adventurer, and world-traveller. In each of these activities there is infinite room for various pleasures, and there are some guilty pleasures that Gordon Ramsay cannot stop himself from indulging in. Devouring A Duck’s Fetus We have seen Gordon all around the world on The Great Escape , and most trips include him eating something that was bizarre, to say the least. He has eaten everything from tarantulas to ant eggs. This one beats them all. On his trip to Cambodia, the same in which he ate the tarantula, Gordon ate a duck's fetus. That's right. Gordon opened a duck's egg, dug out its 20-day old unborn baby and swallowed it. At first he was hesitant, of course, but after eating it, he actually enjoyed that duck fetus. There is another pleasure involved in this too. According to Gordon's guide, duck fetuses enhance a man's sex life. Whether it does enhance your sex life or not, and even if it is delicious, the fact remains that this is a fetus. This could very well be Gordon's guiltiest pleasure. Eating Stuffed Frogs Another exotic but somewhat cold-hearted meal that Gordon found his ultimate pleasure in was stuffed frogs. It was on the same trip to Cambodia where he ate the duck fetus, but we probably know by now how Gordon is up for tasting any kind of food no matter how weird it sounds or looks. During the night, Gordon and some of his Cambodian companions went on a frog hunt by the river, and after catching a few decently-sized frogs, they headed back to the shack for the grill. First, they killed the frogs, gutted them then prepared the stuffing. Using minced pork meat mixed with a traditional Cambodian spice paste called Kroeung, they stuffed the frogs before putting them on the grill. In a small supper gathering, Gordon got to taste his first serving of stuffed frogs, and he just sounded amazed by the taste. Fresh Eels In Breadcrumbs For most of us who haven't tried them before, eels are probably attributed in our heads with slime or ugly jelly. Gordon doesn't like that. Eels are not that popular in Britain, and Gordon loves them so much that he wanted to change this. He not only finds them delicious, he even thinks they are part of an abandoned heritage. In one of his episodes on The F Word , Gordon met with the only commercial eel fisherman left in order to see how eels are found. He then cooked a test sample for people to try, and his eels in breadcrumbs recipe looks good enough to change our minds about eels. It certainly impressed the people who tasted it. By the way, eels are considered a fine delicacy in the Netherlands, and that is what Gordon wants to make them in Britain and the US. Making Tripe Great Again Many young people might think tripe is gross alien like flesh extracted from the cattle’ stomachs, and they're absolutely right. But this weird looking meat is actually a traditional delicacy in Britain. Old people seem to love it, and so does master chef Gordon Ramsay. When Gordon visited a butcher, he got to meet a bunch of 60+ year old people who shared his tripe indulgence. He actually met people who ate tripe raw with only some sauce on the top or even just salt and vinegar. There was an old man that was buying the tripe to eat it as a snack! Gordon didn't like the fact that only old people were enjoying tripe, so he used one of his magic recipes to add some modern spirit to this strange piece of meat. He then got a line of young boys to taste it and apparently his recipe was a hit with them. Roasting People This one is not a surprise for anybody. If there are two things that define Gordon Ramsay, they are extraordinary cooking skills and a foul mouth. Serve Gordon bad food and you will get roasted. Keep your restaurant a dirty mess and you will get roasted. Just hang out with Gordon and you will have some curse words coming at you. Roasts are so iconic of Gordon that some of his fans would pay money to have them roast them. As a matter of fact, one of Gordon's campaigns called Ramsay's Great British Roast included interactive street posters where Gordon made a live appearance and kept roasting random people on the streets of Brighton who he watched through cameras pinned to the posters. He roasted them for their looks, and most importantly, for whatever food they carried around that he found subpar or just outright disgusting. The people weren’t even upset about it. Gordon’s roasts are probably even more popular than his food. Gordon loses his mind over some caviar There are very few things that can please Gordon like a nice serving of caviar. He once flew to Spain to visit a caviar farm over there, and you can rarely see Gordon in such an ecstatic mood. When he and his guide came out with the fish that they caught and went to have the caviar extracted from it, Gordon could not contain his amazement. He took the caviar right out of the fish's belly and ate it. His mind was blown by the amount of caviar they found inside one fish, which was worth around 10,000 pounds. After having it processed, Gordon took his can of caviar and split with a wide smile. He then made a lobster dish with a side of potato salad with that exquisite caviar he brought with him from Spain. He called it the perfect dish for the last supper and it certainly looked like it. Beasting it up It's a given that Gordon Ramsay looks pretty good for his age. A man over 50 who is that buff is an almost rare find. If we consider the fact that he is a chef who is surrounded 24/7 with all types of mouthwatering food including his own, his ability to maintain such a physique becomes more and more impressive. That physique does not come easily, though. One of the things in which Gordon completely loses himself in is sports. For one, he has run the London marathon more than once, and has entered into triathlon competitions. That is, of course, besides his normal workout routine. That makes him capable of eating well while maintaining good health and staying in good shape. When he appeared on The Jimmy Kimmel Show , Kimmel was intimidated by his hand shake! Not only are sports an essential part of Gordon's life, he even makes sure that his wife and children are athletic as well. Exploring the world We have seen Gordon in many countries all over the globe. Travelling is actually an essential part of Gordon's life. Beyond the obvious reasons why travelling might be appealing, like expanding one's experiences and knowledge of the world, getting in touch with various cultures, and so on, travelling has had a magnificent effect on Gordon's career. He says that his first trip to Paris completely changed his idea about his cooking skills because it made him realize how much he did not know about food. Gordon has been pretty fond of featuring different cuisines from around the world, and on his travel show, The Great Escape, he has taken us with him on trips to many countries to let us see their cuisine and the methods they use in cooking. He's been to different corners of the globe, from Finland to Spain to Cambodia, and from every journey he comes back with more and more to add to his magic in the kitchen. The “Wake up, you donkey” cocktail It's hard to be such a master of taste like Gordon is and not have cocktails on your list of guilty pleasures. When he appeared on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon , the master chef had a glass of his favourite cocktail with his host. It included tequila, cider, smoked elderflower, and fresh honey. If you think that it's a fancy drink, wait till you hear its name. That magnificent cocktail is called "Wake up, you donkey," and it is served at the Gordon Ramsay Pub & Grill in Atlantic City. Gordon is definitely a bit nit picky when it comes to food, and we don't think he's any different with drinks. That must be one hell of a drink to have won Gordon's heart like that. Gordon loves his Ferrari collection Gordon is an absolute Ferrari maniac. If you follow Gordon on social media, you probably know how insane he is about his two-strong LaFerrari collection. He first had his coupe LaFerrari, then in late 2016 he got his new LaFerrari, this time a convertible Aperta, one of only 499 units to be sold of this model. Gordon has pledged to add a new Ferrari to his collection with every coming Michelin star he receives. Gordon is no conservative driver either. He has worked his tricks on America's radars by wrapping his license plates in cling film in order to reflect the flash from the radar's cameras, so instead of doing the 70mph speed limit on Los Angeles highways, he can enjoy his car's stunning speed that is triple that limit. Although he's a 51 year old father, when it comes to his Ferraris Gordon still has the spirit of a child. He's so protective of them, yet looks for any chance to show them off. He is a real Disney enthusiast Maybe one would not guess it from his rough nature and his dead seriousness, but Gordon is actually a real enthusiast of Disney movies. In a Reddit: Ask Me Anything thread that Gordon started a couple of years ago, he was asked which Disney movie was his favourite, and he chose Ratatouille . This is not the only Disney chef that Gordon loves, - he has voiced a couple of animated chef characters himself. He played a chef on an episode of Phineas and Ferb , has challenged the Swedish Chef on the Food Fight “ Muppisode”, and he voices chef Oxley on Mickey and the Roadster Racers which has just recently started airing. Chef Oxley is actually modeled after Gordon himself. With blonde hair similar to Gordon's, Chef Oxley goes to restaurants to give them a shake up and help their crews to get things in order. To suit the show's young audience, though, chef Oxley does so without Gordon's iconic cursing. Scrambled eggs throughout the day Eggs are one of the things that Gordon has made over and over on his shows. Burgers, steaks and eggs, have had perhaps the most frequent appearances with Gordon. He particularly loves his eggs scrambled. In the same Reddit: Ask Me Anything thread, Gordon was asked about how he liked his eggs, and his answer was... scrambled. He thinks scrambled eggs are a meal that fits into any slot in the day. One can eat them at breakfast, in the afternoon, as a 5 pm snack, or in the evening. He also finds scrambled eggs to be a perfect weekend breakfast, and with the way he makes them, they definitely are the perfect breakfast. Although they are a simple and time efficient meal, Gordon still thinks scrambled eggs are something of an art. He definitely manages to make a fine dish out of the simplest types of food, and scrambled eggs are no exception. Social Media Presence Gordon Ramsay's social media presence is powerful. If you are a fan of the masteryou can get to know all about his life, family, cars and his global adventures. Gordon posts regularly on Twitter, Facebook, Instagram and, of course, YouTube where all of his professional content is posted. A huge part of Gordon's roasts occur via Twitter in particular, where Gordon hunts down inferior chefs and hecklers with his typical intimidating, witty attitude. It is not all roasts and insults though. Via Twitter, Gordon opens the door for questions and ideas from his fans where he does take these messages seriously and tries to answer them. If you are going to holler at Gordon via social media, know that you might be up for your fair share of mockery. Occasional Fast Food Indulgences It might shock many people to hearGordon is a real fan of fast food.mind that he clearly distinguishesjunk. Gordon is a chef after all, and there is maybe nothing more appalling to a chef than grease infested junk food. Gordon has some pretty tough standards if he is going to eat fast food. He is disgusted by McDonald’s, for example. There are pizzas that he might enjoy, and he apparently loves In N' Out burgers where he finds the meat to be delicious and he's delighted by the fact that the fries are hand cut right in front of you. Although he has his occasional fast food indulgences, Gordon is still strict about maintaining his physique, and even his family's physique. He allows his kids some fast food, but it's only once every few weeks and the poor kids have to go out for a run before school if they'll be having some during the day. It's not a surprise to anyone that Gordon is such a harsh parent, though. Hunting down his own food As we've seen, Gordon has been to so many places, and in each of the countries he visited, there were one or more animals that are not traditionally eaten in the west and which Gordon wanted to give a try and many times he had to find them himself. While in Cambodia, Gordon went down to the river to hunt the frogs that he ate, but that wasn't the only time he went to capture the prey. While in Iceland, Gordon went on a hunt for puffins, which are cute bulky Icelandic birds that apparently make for good food. We have seen him hunting for Burmese pythons in Florida, casually going on a Lionfish hunt and he went hand-diving for scallops while in Britain. Gordon's adventures hunting for food are just as exciting as his Kitchen Nightmares visits and his normal journeys around the world. GR just knows how to keep the action coming. We bet you were flabbergasted by some of these insane guilty pleasure. At least we were! What are some of your guilty pleasures? Sound off in the comments below and don’t forget to hit that subscribe button and notification bell.

Blade Runner 2049 is a complex and amazing film and there are a ton of little nods and inside moments in this film so we wanted to share a few of our favorite Blade Runner 2049 easter eggs that you may have missed. And while Blade runner 2049 takes place in the far flung future. We would love to be part of your present by you hitting that subscribe button and dining that little notification bell as well. A dog joke? Blade Runner 2049 is set a ways in the future and is a extension of the world in the original blade runner. Although things have progress. They haven't made the moves you would like for a movie that takes place 30 years after the original. That includes in the replicants as well. In the first film Deckard is chasing the Nexus 6 model replicants and nearly 30 years later we have only moved up 3 full revisions to the Nexus 9 Which is what our protagonist K is. It looks like their biggest upgrade is the removal of their freedom and their names. And the fact that his name is K and he is a nexus 9 is kind of hard not to make the dog connection. His full name ‘KD9-3.7’ So let me get this The hero in our movie is a loyal lapd Nexus 9 with Letter designation K Come on now. Not really the most high brow joke or reference but we think that is more than just a coincidence. Skin Jobs Blade Runner 2049 does a pretty solid job at showing that Replicants are second class citizens. From the sideways glances from the people of LA to the slurs used for replicants which seemed to have been a holdover all the way from 2019. That being Skinjob or the variation Skinner. First uttered by Police Chief Harry Bryant when he and Deckard meet at the LAPD headquarters. In 2049 in the first lab scene the forensic scientist CoCo calls replicants skinjobs and on K’s apartment the word skinner is spray painted on his door. A neat little world building building easter egg showing that people are still pretty hateful towards artificial beings. Deckards LAPD Blaster It takes a good long while for us to even get a glimpse of Harrison Fords Deckard in Blade Runner 2049. Seriously he shows up at the tail end of the second act almost 90 mins into the film. When we do meet him it is in orange tinted and potentially radiated ruins of Las Vegas. He gets the drop on K while he is messing with Deckard's piano. In the reveal we get to see the aged and haggard Deckard bare down on K with a weapon drawn. That weapon? His official LAPD 2019 Blaster pistol from the original Blade Runner. Even after all this time and advancement. Deckard still prefers his original gun from his time as a Blade Runner. Phillip K Dick Reference In The Early Portion of the film Agent K is tracking down the origins of some Nexus 7 bones and is looking for any type of lead he can get. This leads to a cameo by Edward James Olmos’ Blade Runner Gaff. No longer the Suave and Stylish Blade Runner. Now Gaff is in an assisted living home. During the conversation Gaff informs K as much as he can about the information that he is seeking and at the end of their conversation he puts down some of his trademark origami. Only this time it is a sheep. A direct reference to the Philip K Dick novel. Do androids dream of electric sheep. The book on which the original Blade Runner takes place. A tiny bit of a two-fer here. While talking to K he goes back and forth between english and city speak. Which he used in the first film. K/ Joe living the Voigt Kompff questions The Voight-Kampff Test is they way Blade Runners determined whether a person of interest was human or replicant in the first film. In 2049 they have a portable eye scanner which can tell instantly whether someone is or is not replication. But back in 2019 they had no such device and relied on the arduous task of the voigt Kompff test. Oddly enough the Voigt Kompff test questions from the first film seem to come to life in the second act of the sequel. With one of the questions referring to a sandy desert which parallels with K walking through the Las Vegas desert. To the more famous question which Deckard asks Rachael about a wasp crawling on her arm. Which is paralleled by K encountering the beehive and have a bees crawling on his arm. And interesting character moment here. In the Voigt Kompff test Rachael responds very quickly that she would kill the wasp on her arm whereas the more obedient Nexus 9 replicant K has no violent tendency towards the bees crawling on his hand and seemling just looks at them. Coke is here to stay There is a metric ton of product placement in Blade Runner 2049 and while that is thematically correct with the first film. Most of the adverts have changed over the years. With Atari Logos becoming these huge traffic framing signs and pan am logos popping up in the cityscape. Only one advert has never changed and that is the giant coca-cola sign which is roughly 100 feet tall if you look at the spinners flying by it. While an awesome easter egg Ridley Scott when asked about the inclusion of the Coke sign in the original film. He simply said of course Coke would be there “Even in a dystopian world Coca-Cola is everlasting” a point which 2049 director Dennis Villeneuve must have taken to heart when he included that exact same advertisement in his film which takes place 30 years later. But not to be left out in the cold parent company Sony made sure to include their products everywhere as to show they also would stand the test of time. The Tyrell Pyramid The tyrell company was the pinnacle of corporate excess in the 2019 and nothing is more evident of that than their gigantic pyramid adorning the Los Angeles skyline. After the events of the original Blade Runner the company continues on for a while before plummeting and going bankrupt. The great Blackout pretty much seals their fate and Niander Wallace swoops in and buys what is left of the company. Converting the great Tyrell Pyramid into his company's headquarters. Thus keeping the great LA pyramid a fixture of the skyline for many years to come. There is also a throw away reference to the Tyrell corporation's motto in Blade Runner 2049. That motto fo course is “More Human than Human” She Had Green Eyes In the third act of the film Deckard is apprehended by Niander Wallace and brought to the Wallace Corporation's headquarters where Wallace attempts to get Deckard to come over to his side by showing him a recreation of his Nexus 7 love Rachael. At first it looks as though Deckard is weakening in his resolve at the prospect of being reunited with a version of Rachael. Until he stops and tells off Wallace that Rachael had green eyes. But here is the rub. She didn't have green eyes they were dark brown. Which raises all sorts of questions about Deckard's memories. But that will have to wait for another time. 2049 opens the way Blade Runner was scripted to The original script for Blade Runner began with a pot of soup boiling on a stove in a farm house kitchen. A heavy-set character asks Deckard if he would like some before the man attacks deckard without warning, Decakrd kills the heavy set man without explanation. This would have been a pretty electrifying opening to the original Blade Runner but was eventually scrapped from the Voigt Kompff opening. In 2049 though it looks like Denis Villeneuve wanted to pay homage to that original opening by including many of the core elements. Including opening on a boiling pot and having a sequence with a larger man. Although in this version it's the muscle bound Sapper Morton played by Dave bautista as opposed to a heavy set man and instead of Deckard it is our new protagonist K. They have a short chat and before you know it Sapper attacks K out of nowhere and leads to a Sapper being retired. This is a really cool moment for die hard Blade Runner fans to see what the original movies opening would look like recreated and used in the sequel. The Pale Fire After K has retired Sapper Morton, he returns to the LAPD headquarters where is required to complete a Post-Trauma Baseline Test to ensure he wasn't emotionally compromised by his most recent mission. Something which can lead to disaterous results for a replicant It appears that this baseline test is standard procedure for Blade Runners in the LAPD by the number of suites that exist after K exits his first baseline test. The Baseline procedure has the subject recite words like 'cell' and 'interlinked' in response to a string of prompts. It comes off sounding like gibberish, but it's actuality it is poetry, taken from the book Pale Fire by Vladimir Nabokov which is chocked full of existential musings much like Blade Runner or the book Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep. Several of K’s prompts are taken from this passage in Pale Fire. And blood-black nothingness began to spin A system of cells interlinked within cells interlinked within cells interlinked within one stem. And dreadfully distinct Against the dark, a tall white fountain played. The choice to use Pale Fire must have been deliberate as the story of the book centers around a fictitious poe, and its editor. Playing with the idea of what is real, what is not, and who gets to decide. Ironically The book appears in K’s apartment and K’s AI girlfriend Joi hates it. And that’s the list. What did we miss ?
